provenance.note: Thomas Butts, Jr., who engraved the plate; probably by inheritance in 1862 to his son, Frederick J. Butts (1833-1905); probably among the collection of Butts family drawings and engravings which, according to Geoffrey Keynes, *Bibliotheca Bibliographici* (London: Trianon Press, 1964) 86, "was obtained from the Butts family by the late Joseph Horne and was bought at his sale about 1954 by Mr. E. Guntrip of Maidstone, who sold it to me [Keynes] in 1961; given by Keynes by bequest in 1982 to the Fitzwilliam Museum, which accessioned the work in 1985.

illustration.illusobjdesc: There are two figures in the print, both of them depicted only by the head, neck, and one with a hint of his shoulders. Based on their short hair and the title of this print, they are two male children. The head on the left is seen in profile, facing left. Due to the dark shading or swelling on his eye, nose, above his lips, chin, jaw and near his ear, he probably has some kind of disease, perhaps Graves' disease, or exophthalmic goiter. The figure on the right is facing forward and has swelling underneath his left eye or eye socket. Though not as afflicted, he to probably has a disease, possibly blepharoadenoma, a tumor of the lower eyelid.

component.illusobjdesc: The head on the left is male and likely a child. Only his head, neck, and the top of his left shoulder, and a sliver of his right shoulder, are visible. He is seen in profile, facing left. He has short, slightly curly hair. Due to the dark shading or swelling on his eye, nose, above his lips, chin, jaw and near his ear, he probably has some kind of disease, perhaps Graves' disease, or exophthalmic goiter.

The figure to the right is male and also a child. He has short, curly hair. His head is facing forward and has swelling underneath his left eye or eye socket. Though not as afflicted as his companion, he probably has some disease, possibly blepharoadenoma, a tumor of the lower eyelid.
